heroHeadline: PLA 6 Sorties May 22 (All Cross N/SW/E ADIZ); 10 PLAN Vessels — Post-Summit Naval High; US FMS Pause Revealed (Operation Epic Fury); China Blocks Colby Beijing Visit Over $14B Arms; HIMARS Deadline May 31 (9 Days)
heroSubtitle: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 6 PLA aircraft sorties on May 22 — all crossing the median line into northern, southwestern, and eastern ADIZ sectors — paired with 10 PLAN vessels operating around Taiwan simultaneously, the highest naval count of the post-Trump-Xi-summit period and the highest since the Liaoning carrier transit on April 20 (12 vessels). The post-summit May sortie sequence now reads: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7→6. While air activity has moderated from the May 20 24-sortie spike (13 crossing N/C/SW/E ADIZ simultaneously), PLA's elevated maritime presence signals a shift toward sustained naval pressure as a primary gray-zone vector as the May 31 HIMARS payment deadline approaches (9 days). On the diplomatic front, US Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao publicly confirmed a temporary pause on foreign military sales while prioritizing munitions for Operation Epic Fury (the ongoing US-Iran operation): 'It's just right now we're doing a pause.' Taiwan's Presidential Office immediately responded that it has 'not received any relevant information about the U.S. adjusting these military sales' and remains 'optimistic.' Simultaneously, reporting revealed that China has blocked Elbridge Colby's planned Pentagon Beijing visit, explicitly linking the visa denial to whether Trump approves the $14 billion PAC-3/NASAMS Taiwan arms package — assessed as Beijing's attempt to delay any arms decision until after Xi Jinping's planned late-September Washington visit. Taiwan's Cabinet formally rejected Trump's claim that America 'lost' its semiconductor industry to Taiwan 'through theft,' with Secretary-General Xavier Chang declaring: 'Taiwan did not steal chips from the world. It supplies them to the world.' Taiwan's US representative Alexander Yui stated: 'We want to keep our way of life as is, and we will not budge.' The HIMARS Finance Committee hearings are scheduled for Monday May 25 with a floor vote expected Wednesday-Thursday May 27-28. The interlocking pressure triangle — $14B package frozen, FMS pause for Iran operations, Colby visit blocked — represents the most complex US arms ambiguity Taiwan has faced in the post-summit period.
